SHA-2 has no structural break; the verdict depends on digest length because Grover reduces preimage cost to 2^(n/2) and BHT-style collision search is bounded by the classical 2^(n/2) birthday bound. A 256-bit digest gives 128-bit collision resistance classically and a 128-bit preimage margin under Grover; CNSA 2.0 requires SHA-384 or larger for national security systems, so this is adequate for integrity today but is not the CNSA 2.0 target.
